mcqs.question: Why can't a plain inverted index match a query for "affordable place to eat" against a document that says "budget-friendly restaurant"?
options: The document is too short to be indexed at all
An inverted index matches literal shared terms, and these two phrases share no words in common
Inverted indexes can only store one document per term
The query has too many words for the index to process
mcqs.explanation: Term matching only works when the same word appears in both the query and the document — these phrases are semantically similar but share zero literal terms, which an inverted index alone can't bridge. Document length and word count aren't the actual limitation.

mcqs.question: Why does exact nearest-neighbor search over vectors not scale to billions of documents?
options: It requires computing the distance from the query to every stored vector, which is a full scan on every query
Vectors longer than 100 dimensions cannot be compared at all
Exact search only works for text, never for images
It requires rebuilding the entire vector index on every query
mcqs.explanation: True nearest-neighbor search checks the query against every vector in the collection, which is a full scan that gets slower as the collection grows — exactly why ANN algorithms like HNSW trade a little accuracy for sub-linear query time. Dimensionality and data type aren't the blocker, and no rebuild happens per query.

mcqs.question: A search product needs to handle both conceptual queries ("cozy winter reads") and exact-identifier queries (a specific product SKU). What approach best serves both?
options: Pure keyword search only, and drop vector search entirely
Pure vector search only, since embeddings capture all query types
Whichever of the two returns results first, per query
Hybrid search — run both keyword and vector queries and merge/re-rank the combined results
mcqs.explanation: Hybrid search combines keyword search's strength on exact identifiers with vector search's strength on conceptual, paraphrased queries, covering both cases a single approach would miss. Racing them by speed doesn't address correctness for either query type.

mcqs.question: A team fully replaces keyword search with pure vector search, and power users complain that searching for exact SKU codes now returns worse results than before. What's the root cause?
options: Embeddings capture semantic similarity, not exact identity, so they have no strong notion of "meaning" for an arbitrary identifier string
Vector search cannot be deployed in production at all
The embedding model was trained on too much data
SKU codes are always too long for any search system to index
mcqs.explanation: Embeddings are built to capture conceptual similarity, not to preserve exact-match precision for identifiers a model was never trained to distinguish — this is exactly why keyword fallback or hybrid search matters. Vector search works fine in production generally, and the other options aren't real constraints.
